findings.issue: USER_REFERRAL_IP_RETENTION is documented as 'Blank is a startup error' (also environment-variables.md:131), but an empty env var resolves the placeholder to an empty string, binds to a null Duration and the setter is skipped, so the field keeps 30d (UserPropertiesValidationTest#blankEnvKeepsDefault proves it). The null check in validateReferral is a defensive guard and its '(it is blank)' message is misleading.
findings.fix: Docs: 'Blank keeps the default (30d)'; reword the requireDuration message to '... must not be null'.

findings.issue: SERVER_FORWARD_HEADERS_STRATEGY=none on the gateway changes what XForwardedHeadersFilter appends for proto and port (http/80 after the ALB's https/443). auth-service reads only the first value, so the Google callback should stay https/443 while the ALB keeps sending X-Forwarded-Proto/Port; not testable here. It also touches the gateway, a requirements non-goal (config only, requested by security).
findings.fix: Post-deploy check of the Google sign-in callback URL on AWS in the PR notes; record the gateway Helm change as a scope deviation in objective.md.

summary: Approve: no blocker or major, every AC met. Round-2 findings resolved (verify output at this SHA recorded; retention <= 0 skips the purge with a WARN and a test; null-duration checks run after binding; AC-13 corrected). Security's NATIVE major addressed: user-service forward-headers-strategy none, gateway SERVER_FORWARD_HEADERS_STRATEGY=none in Helm, trusted hops 3 = gateway 2 + 1. ReferralForwardedForTomcatTest distinguishes fix from old behaviour (under NATIVE the RemoteIpValve would rewrite the header and hop 3 would be the spoofed entry). The engineer's 'blank keeps the default' claim is correct; only the env docs are wrong (minor). Client-IP duplication tracked as B-1.
